BiblicalUsage: Twice, in the same proverb repeated word for word: The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly. The word is to sip up, to swallow down — gossip goes down like a dainty morsel, swallowed whole, and settles in the deepest place.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for sipping up carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the proverb, repeated twice because the warning needs repeating, that gossip is swallowed and settles deep.
